title: The LaPorte Congressman Who Went to Expose a Seance

sources.what: Cathcart, judge and ex-congressman turned spiritualist; originally a skeptic, attended his first spirit circle at the home of Mr. Poston of La Porte County to expose fraud; brought a homemade flash device; a spirit called 'old king' took up a bass drum; his Spiritual Telegraph account: '[I] witnessed the stick beating the drum as if handled from above, and no mortal nearer than about eight feet of it!'; became a convert and started his own spirit circle in LaPorte County
sources.who: Indiana Historical Bureau, Talking Hoosier History, 'Spiritualism: Beyond the Spectacle' (2019)

sources.what: Emma Hardinge's history describes a spirit room of the Poston circle in Indiana and Charles Cathcart's spirit room in the same state
sources.who: Transatlantica (journal), 'Des maisons hantees en Amerique au XIXe siecle', citing Hardinge, Modern American Spiritualism (1870)

sources.what: chapter 'Cathcart's Spirit Room', named for Charles Cathcart, ex-Congressman from La Porte, in an 1870 spiritualist book
sources.who: Indiana Historical Society, 'Spooky Selections from the Library' (2018)

sources.what: Charles W. Cathcart (1809-1888): farmed near La Porte, Indiana Senate 1837-40, U.S. House 1845-49, U.S. Senate Dec. 6, 1852-Jan. 18, 1853; died on his farm near La Porte
sources.who: Wikipedia, Charles W. Cathcart; Biographical Directory of the U.S. Congress

sources.what: Western Spiritualism continued, Indiana. Cathcart's spirit room (chapter 32)
sources.who: Hardinge, Modern American Spiritualism (1870), table of contents

sources.what: Ohio-style spirit rooms: the spirit 'King', bass drum played by spirits

beats.text: In the dark, a drum began to beat. And a former congressman from LaPorte had come to prove it was a trick.
beats.label: LAPORTE COUNTY, THE 1800s

beats.text: His name was Charles Cathcart. He farmed near LaPorte, served in Congress, and briefly in the United States Senate.
beats.label: CHARLES CATHCART
beats.credit: Biographical Directory of the U.S. Congress · AI-generated picture

beats.text: He didn't believe in spirit circles. So he went to one at the Poston home, to expose it.
beats.label: A LAPORTE COUNTY HOME

beats.text: He brought a homemade device that could light the dark room in a flash.
beats.label: HIS TRAP

beats.text: The lights went out. A spirit the circle called Old King began to beat a bass drum.
beats.label: OLD KING

beats.text: Cathcart hit his light. He wrote that the stick beat the drum as if from above, with no one within about eight feet.
beats.label: WHAT HE WROTE

lines: ...the stick beating the drum as if handled from above,
and no mortal nearer than about eight feet of it!

beats.credit: His account in the Spiritual Telegraph, via Indiana Historical Bureau

beats.text: The skeptic became a believer, and started a spirit circle of his own.
beats.label: CATHCART'S SPIRIT ROOM

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.
